text:
Maya: leaving shift now — quick sunset pass summary so the overnight team can pick up. Short version: two pagers (kv-cache pager + routing 429s), partial customer impact for interactive endpoints in us-west for ~30m, mitigations applied (fallback routing + increased per-model token throttle). No ongoing customer-facing errors at the moment, but there is a coverage gap 02:00-04:00 UTC where we don't have a designated secondary on-call. See runbook pointers below.

incident-bot: Pager summary: 1) kv-cache-throttle (P1) triggered 2026-12-16T18:10Z — root cause suspected hot-key eviction from aggressive cache compaction. 2) routing-429s (P2) started 2026-12-16T18:22Z — burst from batcher retries. Relevant traces: https://internal.redwood/trace/abc123

Maya: what I did during the incident: 1) toggled rollback of latest batcher config to v2.1 -> v2.0 (reduced batch size max) 2) set fallback routing policy to route 10% of traffic to smaller model-variant (config snippet below) 3) temporarily raised kv-cache capacity on two affected pools to reduce evictions.

Maya: config snippet (for reference):
```
route_policy:
  - id: fallback-small-variant
    match: region==us-west && model_family==gptx
    weight: 10%
batcher:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048 # rollback to previous
kv_cache:
  pool_size_override: +2
```

Aj: thanks — did we see any customer errors surface (500s or corrupted outputs)?

Maya: brief customer impact: some interactive sessions saw 429s and degraded latency. No 5xx spikes in API edge logs beyond transient retries. Affected customers: two enterprise tenants in us-west (tenant ids masked in ticket). Tickets opened: TKT-4629 (enterprise A, latency), TKT-4630 (enterprise B, transient 429).

Connor: I'm coming on in ~10m as backup — can you call out anything I should watch first?

Maya: yes — please watch these three things: 1) kv-cache eviction rate (metric: infra.kv_cache.evictions_per_min by pool) — alert if > 50/min for > 5m 2) router 429 ratio (metric: infra.router.429_ratio) — if > 1% sustained over 2m, flip fallback weight to 20% and notify me 3) batcher backlog latency (infra.batcher.queue_ms) — if tail > 2s, scale dedicated batchers up.

Maya: runbook pointers: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-evictions (section: emergency-scale) and https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/router-fallback (steps to change weights). Quick CLI commands: `redctl kv set-pool-size --pool us-west-a --delta 2` and `redctl route adjust --policy fallback-small-variant --weight 20%`.

Connor: got it. I'll take primary for 00:00-04:00 UTC tomorrow and try to cover the gap. If anything pages at night and I'm unreachable ping @Tessa as secondary.

Tessa: noted — I'll be available for escalations 01:00-05:00 UTC if Connor needs help.

Aj: is there any follow-up work we should open now so the PMs/customers have visibility?

Maya: yes — open follow-ups: 1) investigate cause of the aggressive compaction that started after the latest autoscaler tune (owner: infra-storage, ticket INF-987) 2) add a synthetic test that exercises hot-key patterns (owner: eng-ml, ticket INF-989) 3) plan a canary for the batcher config change with smaller ramp step (owner: eng-runtime, ticket INF-990). I linked the tickets in the incident doc.

Maya: current status: mitigations applied, metrics returned to baseline after ~25m, no remaining active pages. Remaining risk: brief regression if traffic spikes during US business hours — we should keep fallback weight at 10% for next 12h and monitor.

incident-bot: Incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-149 (contains timeline, RCA notes, and customer comms drafts).

Connor: quick question — do we want me to pre-stage a small model-variant instance pool for us-west to reduce fallback cold-starts? I can spin up 2x low-cost instances now and delete tomorrow morning.

Maya: yes please do that — pre-stage 2 warm instances in us-west-a and tag them `eviction-mitigation`. Use cheap instance type and health-checks. If they're healthy, reduce fallback routing to 5% to test.

Tessa: acknowledged, will watch the tickets and step in if required.

Aj: one operational note for the night crew: if you see router 429s and kv evictions at the same time, prefer scaling kv-pools first (cheaper) before route changes. Also call pager-ops if the combined impact affects >5% of requests.

Maya: leaving a short checklist for whoever relieves Connor: 1) confirm pre-staged instances are healthy, 2) check evictions and router 429s for 30m after any config change, 3) escalate to eng-runtime if batcher queue_ms tail > 2.5s.

Connor: ack — I'll post an update in the morning with metrics snapshot and any overnight anomalies.

Maya: thanks team, logging off now. :wave:

sre-bot: Automated summary posted to #incidents: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-149/summary — includes attached graphs and ETA for follow-ups.

Connor: signing off in thread — I'm primary until 04:00 UTC. Ping me with @Connor for urgent pages.

Tessa: will stand by for escalations. Good luck and thanks. :thumbsup:
